scope: Theorem 5.5 (Planar dot-product alternative) of the manuscript “Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension” (preprints/Every-four-dimensional-Kakeya-set-has-full-Hausdorff-dimension-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 30d0c186aa9c697d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 76. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every ε > 0 there are η, δ0 > 0 such that the following holds for 0 < p ≤ δ0. Let A, B ⊂ [0, 1]2, and suppose that Ns(E ∩ B(z, w)) ≤ p−η w/s for E ∈ {A, B}, p ≤ s ≤ w. (5.17) At least one of the following alternatives holds: 1. There are affine lines ℓ, ℓ⊥ with perpendicular directions such that both Np(A ∩ {z : dist(z, ℓ) ≤ p}), Np(B ∩ {z : dist(z, ℓ⊥ ) ≤ p}) are at least pε−1. 2. Every restricted triple set H ⊂ A × B × B with Np(H) ≥ pη−3 admits a scale s ≥ p and an interval J, |J| ≥ p−ηs, for which Ns J ∩ {a · (b − b′ ) : (a, b, b′ ) ∈ H}  ≥ (|J|/s)1−ε .
